note: Encounter setting per visit. Evidence is ranked, not added up: the highest non-empty tier decides alone. tier1 = the page's own matched page type that exists in one setting only, keyed on page_taxonomy.json sub-type names, else page type names. tier2 = text that names the setting. tier3 = hints that also occur in other settings; they only break a tie inside the deciding tier. context phrases are logged and never score. A negative removes the tier 2/3 finding it names (cancels) or every tier 2/3 finding of a setting (cancels_setting). A phrase is recorded once per visit however often it appears. Lower priority wins a tie. Reloads on change. 2026-10-20 (user): follow-up / return / established / new-patient / wellness visits are tier 2 Outpatient (F2F); more tele, inpatient and home phrases.

confidence.note: 2026-10-25 (user: no fixed confidences): how strongly keyword evidence BACKS a setting, not a confidence. A page's confidence is the encounter model's probability for its setting (normalised over the settings, 'No evidence on page' left out), lifted by this support (stages/lib/confidence.py: p + (1 - p) x 0.5 x support) and penalised for doubt; without a model answer, the support x no_model. See vote.confidence_note.

default.note: 2026-10-20 (user): a visit with no setting evidence, or no usable date, is Outpatient (F2F); decided_by 'default', and reason keeps why (no_setting_evidence / no_date / default_date). Its confidence is a fallback's: the model's probability for F2F on the first page x fallback (0.6), so it is never good. Empty setting = leave it unresolved.

applies_to.note: 2026-10-23 (user): a page whose L1 family is not listed votes Not Applicable (lab, orders, forms...); listed families vote their evidence or their vote.family_defaults. Empty families = every page votes its evidence. 2026-10-25 (user): shown as Not Available. 2026-10-25 (user): the encounter's document type decides first: a family in 'always' is that setting whatever its pages say (Discharge Summary, Operative Note -> Inpatient); a family not listed is Not Applicable for the whole encounter, even when one of its pages votes a setting.

negatives.phrase: follow up with your primary care

vote.note: 2026-10-25 (user): the encounter's FIRST PAGE decides when it has evidence of its own (tier 1 page type, tier 2 phrase, or the encounter model: decided_by first_page). Only when it cannot (Not Applicable, its family default, or nothing) do the pages vote -- only those with evidence of their own; the family defaults (Progress Note -> F2F) only when no page has any: the first page counts first_page_weight times; Not Applicable wins only when every vote is Not Applicable; otherwise the weighted majority of the settings wins (a tie goes to the first page's vote), confidence = the winner's share of the weight.
vote.confidence_note: 2026-10-25 (user: a percentage, model probability penalised, one scale: >= 0.80 good, 0.50-0.80 passable, < 0.50 review). Each page's vote: the encounter model's probability for the setting (normalised over the settings), lifted by the keyword support behind it (tier 1 page type 1.0, tier 2 phrase 0.8, 0.8 / 0.6 with a conflict on the page, a confirm word 0.5), x keywords_disagree (0.7) when the model's own answer (>= 0.5) is another setting or the vote overrode a phrase; a family default (Progress Note -> F2F): the model's probability for it x fallback (0.6); Not Applicable: the model's probability backed fully by the page type. Without a model answer: the support x no_model (0.85). The encounter's: the first page's own when it decides (x conflict 0.8 when another page with evidence disagrees); for a vote, the winner's share of the weight x the weighted mean confidence of the pages that voted for it. Penalties: keyword-canon/confidence_canon.json.

model_vote.note: 2026-10-25 (encounter model retrained on the page target, user: keywords must not block): the model votes for a page with no tier 1 / tier 2 evidence of its own, before its family default, for Evisit, Home Visit and Inpatient. A setting gets the vote when the model gives it >= min_confidence (0.5) -- its top answer or not -- or, with one of the setting's confirm words on the page, >= confirm_min (0.3): the keyword lowers the bar, it never blocks. Measured on the retrained model's held-out pages (val + test): Evisit 7 of 7 right at >= 0.3 (4 pages the rules miss), Home Visit 2 of 2, Inpatient 28 of 37 at >= 0.5 (21 right beyond the rules) and 32 of 43 with a keyword at >= 0.3. F2F and Not Available stay with the rules. Small samples: re-measure on new charts.
model_vote.classes_note: Every setting's class in the encounter model, for the confidence of whatever was decided (model vote or not).
model_vote.confirm_note: The confirm words lower the model's bar to confirm_min; they never block a model vote (2026-10-25, user).

override_f2f_phrase.note: 2026-10-25 (user): a model answer at very high confidence beats a weak page phrase. When the page's only evidence is a tier 2 phrase for F2F ('office visit', 'clinic note': template wording that also sits on telehealth and home visits) and the model says Evisit, Home Visit or Inpatient at >= 0.95, the model's setting wins (by model_override). Only F2F phrases are overridden: a phrase for any other setting ('inpatient', 'telehealth visit') stays. Held-out pages: fires on 4, right on 4; encounter test pages ENC_15 (house call with an 'Office Visit' footer) and ENC_14 (telehealth on an office template).

negatives_note: 2026-10-25 (user, encounter test pages ENC_03 / ENC_09): an ambulatory surgery centre or a same-day discharge home cancels the inpatient evidence, the Operative Note page-type prior included ('tier1': true); 'admitted to medicine', 'accepting physician' and the like are inpatient statements.
tier1_note: 2026-10-25 (user): Emergency Note is not hard-coded to a setting; its pages' evidence and the model decide.
